what_this_is: Tables behind a demo page about New York City restaurant inspections. Scores are violation points: lower is better; 0-13 is an A, 14-27 a B, 28+ a C. Restaurants can contest violations at a city hearing; dismissed violations are removed and the score falls.

what_studies_report: A sick or infectious food worker is the leading factor: 40% to 59% of restaurant outbreaks with known factors (CDC: Lipcsei 2019; Moritz 2023).
Temperature-control violations: about ten times the odds of an outbreak (Seattle: Irwin 1989).
A contamination violation: odds ratio 4.9 (Minnesota: Firestone 2020, in System's public graph).
Evidence of vermin: odds ratio 3.3 in one study (Miami-Dade: Cruz 2001, in System's public graph); pests are not a named factor in CDC outbreak analyses.
Overall inspection scores predicted outbreaks in two studies and not in three.
Our registered test in New York: food-poisoning complaints were 1.12 times as frequent after a poor score (0.96 to 1.32), unsettled, because noise complaints rose 1.67 times.
limits: Exploratory analysis from 14 November 2026, not refereed.
The copies show what changed, not why; hearings are the likely cause.
Removals are rare: 1.5% of all violations, and under 2% for each of the four groups, though a few single codes reach 4% to 6%.
Cuisine and borough differences are untested and have many possible causes.
There are no records for individual named restaurants in these tables; the page's lookup box handles those.
